::: {.key-question}
Are Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people in the NEPHU catchment living in affordable and suitable housing?
:::

## Housing Suitability

### Overcrowding

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 9](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/housing/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people secure appropriate, affordable housing that is aligned with their priorities and need**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people living in appropriately sized (not overcrowded) housing to 88%.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Overcrowding
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in TableBuilder data
overcrowded_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Household_Overcrowding_LGA.csv",
                                     variable = "overcrowding") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!overcrowding %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable", "Unable to determine")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(overcrowding = dplyr::case_when(
    overcrowding == "Four or more extra bedrooms needed" ~ "No",
    overcrowding == "Three extra bedrooms needed"        ~ "No",
    overcrowding == "Two extra bedrooms needed"          ~ "No",
    overcrowding == "One extra bedroom needed"           ~ "No",
    overcrowding == "No bedrooms needed or spare"        ~ "Yes",
    overcrowding == "One bedroom spare"                  ~ "Yes",
    overcrowding == "Two bedrooms spare"                 ~ "Yes",
    overcrowding == "Three bedrooms spare"               ~ "Yes",
    overcrowding == "Four or more bedrooms spare"        ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling - by LGA
overcrowded_lga <- overcrowded_lga %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = overcrowding,
                       level    = "household",
                       dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 93% (n = 5,654) of households in the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had an adequate number of bedrooms. This was similar to non-Indigenous households in the NEPHU catchment (97%).

- The number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment with an adequate number of bedrooms ranged from 917 (Whittlesea LGA) to 155 (Manningham LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander appropriately sized households and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous households was biggest for Yarra Ranges and Darebin LGAs.

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment with an adequate number of bedrooms (not overcrowded) ranged from 98% (Boroondara LGA) to 91% (Hume LGA).

- All 12 LGAs in the NEPHU catchment were above the Closing the Gap target of 88%.

- Further historical and ongoing target context can be found on the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/housing/).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, it was discussed that these data were thought to be an underestimate of overcrowding. Reasons for possible underreporting of overcrowding included fears of losing social housing or child protection involvement.

- It was also noted however that Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people have a strong culture of supporting each other to address housing needs. 

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following questions were asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Is the person male, female, and/or non-binary?
  - What is the person's date of birth and age?
  - What is the person's relationship to the person completing the Census form for the household?
  - How many bedrooms are there in this dwelling?

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - Responses were cross-tabulated for all household members to assess the number of bedrooms required for the household, based on the [Canadian National Occupancy Standard](https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/386254) for housing appropriateness.
  - Appropriately sized households were defined as those where extra bedrooms were not required.

:::

### Housing Quality

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Housing of acceptable standard
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
suitability_acceptable <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Household_Acceptable.csv")

# Data wrangling
suitability_acceptable <- suitability_acceptable %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(household_living_in_house_of_an_acceptable_standard_n:household_living_in_house_not_of_an_acceptable_standard_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(yes_n = household_living_in_house_of_an_acceptable_standard_n,
                no_n  = household_living_in_house_not_of_an_acceptable_standard_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(yes_n:no_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yes"),
                starts_with("no"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yes"      = "Yes",
                                              "no"       = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Housing - structural issues
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
suitability_structural <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Household_Structural.csv")

# Data wrangling
suitability_structural <- suitability_structural %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(none_n:ten_n)),
                lesstwo_n  = sum(across(none_n:one_n)),
                moretwo_n  = sum(across(two_n:ten_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(yes_n = lesstwo_n,
                no_n  = moretwo_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(yes_n:no_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100,
                #
                category = "Less than two structural issues") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(category,
                sex,
                starts_with("yes"),
                starts_with("no_"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!c(sex, category),
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yes"      = "Yes",
                                              "no"       = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

suitability_combined <- suitability_structural %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(suitability_kitchen) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(suitability_laundry) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(suitability_bathroom) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(suitability_sewerage)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 83% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they were living in a dwelling of an acceptable standard. This equates to approximately 33,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to report living in a dwelling of an acceptable standard than males (85% vs. 81%).

- The most commonly reported housing quality issues by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne were structural issues (15% of survey respondents, approximately 5,800 people) and a lack of adequate facilities for storing and preparing food (7.1% of survey respondents, approximately 2,800 people).

- Males were more likely to report each type of housing quality issue than females.

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following questions were asked of a representative for each household completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey:
  - Does this house have any of these problems that need to be fixed? (Select all that apply)
    - Rising damp
    - Major cracks in walls or floors
    - Sinking or moving foundations
    - Sagging floors
    - Walls or windows that aren't straight
    - Wood rot or termite damage
    - Major electrical problems
    - Major plumbing problems
    - Major roof defects
    - Other major structural problems
  - Are there any of these facilities that this house doesn't have or that are not working? (Select all that apply)
    - Stove, oven, or other cooking facilities
    - Fridge
    - Toilet
    - Bath or shower
    - Washing machine
    - Kitchen sink
    - Laundry tub

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_natsihs`
  - A house or dwelling was of an acceptable standard if there were working facilities for washing people, for washing clothes or bedding, for storing and preparing food, sewerage facilities, and if there were no more than two major structural problems.

:::

```{r}

table <- suitability_combined %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = "sex",

  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", figtab_table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Housing Affordability

### Housing Tenure

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Housing tenure type
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in TableBuilder data
tenure_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Household_Tenure_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "tenure") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!tenure %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(tenure = dplyr::case_when(
    tenure == "Owned outright"        ~ "Owned (outright)",
    tenure == "Owned with a mortgage" ~ "Owned (mortgage)",
    #
    tenure == "Rented" ~ "Rented",
    #
    tenure == "Other"                                  ~ "Other",
    tenure == "Occupied rent free"                     ~ "Other",
    tenure == "Occupied under a life tenure scheme"    ~ "Other",
    tenure == "Purchased under a shared equity scheme" ~ "Other",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# Data wrangling
tenure_lga <- tenure_lga %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = tenure,
                       level    = "household",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(outright_prop = aboriginal_n_owned_outright / aboriginal_total * 100,
                mortgage_prop = aboriginal_n_owned_mortgage / aboriginal_total * 100,
                rented_prop   = aboriginal_n_rented / aboriginal_total * 100,
                other_prop    = aboriginal_n_other / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                outright_n = aboriginal_n_owned_outright,
                outright_prop,
                mortgage_n = aboriginal_n_owned_mortgage,
                mortgage_prop,
                rented_n = aboriginal_n_rented,
                rented_prop,
                other_n = aboriginal_n_other,
                other_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 52% (n = 3,347) of households in the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were renting, 30% (n = 1,910) owned their home with a mortgage, and 16% (n = 989) owned their home outright.

- The percentage of rented households with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander was higher than for non-Indigenous households (52% vs 27%), while the percentage of mortgaged or owned outright homes was lower than for non-Indigenous households (owned with mortgage: 30% vs 38%; owned outright: 16% vs 33%).

- In Darebin (76%) and Yarra (75%) LGAs, higher proportions of households were rented, which may reflect the younger age profile of these LGAs.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Is this dwelling:
    - Owned outright
    - Owned with a mortgage
    - Purchased under a shared equity scheme
    - Rented
    - Occupied rent free
    - Occupied under a life tenure scheme
    - Other

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`

:::

### Housing Stress

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mortgage/rental stress
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in TableBuilder data
mortgage_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Household_Mortgage_LGA.csv",
                                  variable = "stress") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(stress = dplyr::case_when(
    stress == "Households where mortgage repayments are more than 30% of household income" ~ "Mortgage more than 30",
    TRUE ~ "Mortgage less than 30"))

rental_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Household_Rent_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "stress") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!stress %in% c("Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(stress = dplyr::case_when(
    stress == "Households where rent payments are more than 30% of household income" ~ "Rent more than 30",
    TRUE ~ "Rent less than 30"))

# Data wrangling
stress_lga <- mortgage_lga %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(rental_lga) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(stress = dplyr::case_when(
    stress == "Mortgage more than 30" ~ "yes",
    stress == "Rent more than 30"     ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = stress,
                       level    = "household",
                       dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 13% (n = 1,244) of households in the NEPHU catchment with at least one member who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census spent more than 30% of their annual household income on housing costs (mortgage or rent). This was slightly higher than for non-Indigenous households in the NEPHU catchment (11%).

- The number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment that spent more than 30% of their annual household income on housing costs ranged from 203 (Whittlesea LGA) to 28 (Nillumbik LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander households that spent more than 30% of their annual household income on housing costs and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous households was biggest for Darebin and Yarra Ranges LGAs.

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander households in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment that spent more than 30% of their annual household income on housing costs ranged from 14% (Whitehorse and Manningham LGAs) to 9.3% (Boroondara LGA).

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - What is the total of all income the person usually receives?
    - Free text response
  - Is this dwelling:
    - Owned outright
    - Owned with a mortgage
    - Purchased under a shared equity scheme
    - Rented
    - Occupied rent free
    - Occupied under a life tenure scheme
    - Other
  - How much does your household pay for this dwelling?
    - Free text response

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - Responses for each household member were summed to calculate the total weekly household income.
  - This topic includes dwellings owned with a mortgage, purchased under a shared equity scheme, or rented.
  - Mortgage or rental payments greater than 30% of household income may not indicate a household is in financial distress. 
    - Households may choose to live in an area with higher costs due to proximity to work, schooling, or other lifestyle factors. 
    - Higher income households may be able to spend more of their income on housing without this affecting their ability to pay for other costs of living. 
    - Some households may choose to pay more than the minimum required payment in order to pay off a mortgage faster.

:::

### Homelessness

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Homelessness, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
homeless_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Household_Homeless_LGA.csv",
                                  variable = "homeless") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(homeless = dplyr::case_when(
    homeless == "Not applicable" ~ "no",
    TRUE ~ "yes"))  

# Data wrangling
homeless_lga <- homeless_lga %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = homeless,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Homelessness, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
homeless_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Household_Homeless_AgeSex.csv",
                                        variable = "homeless") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(homeless = dplyr::case_when(
    homeless == "Not applicable" ~ "no",
    TRUE ~ "yes")) 

# Data wrangling
homeless_agesex <- homeless_agesex %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = homeless,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 2.2% (n = 264) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census were homeless or marginally housed on Census night. This was higher than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (0.64%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who were homeless or marginally housed on Census night ranged from 64 (Darebin LGA) to 0 (Nillumbik LGA).

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who were homeless or marginally housed on Census night and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Darebin, Yarra Ranges, and Whittlesea LGAs.

- The percentage of people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who were homeless or marginally housed on Census night ranged from 4.5% (Whitehorse LGA) to 0.0% (Nillumbik LGA).

- There were a higher number of homeless or marginally housed females compared to males, particularly in the 40-49 year age group.

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who were homeless or marginally housed on Census night and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for people aged less than 20 years and people aged 40-49 years for both males and females.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Where does the person usually live?
    - Free text response

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - *Homeless* was defined as people who were living in improvised dwellings, tents, or sleeping out; living in supported accommodation for the homeless; staying temporarily with other households; living in boarding houses; living in severely crowded dwellings; or living in other temporary lodgings on Census night.
  - *Marginally housed* was defined as people who were living in other (not severely) crowded dwellings, living in other improvised dwellings, or marginally housed in caravan parks on Census night.

:::
